stem: Which statement best defines juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA)?

options.text: Persistent joint swelling for more than 6 weeks in a child under 16 years, without a defined cause
Any painful joint in a child under 18 years
Any arthritis lasting more than 2 weeks if inflammatory markers are raised
Recurrent joint pain after exercise in a hypermobile child
A child with night pain that improves with NSAIDs

explanation: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis is defined as persistent joint swelling for more than 6 weeks in a child under 16 years, with no defined cause.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis

rationale: The key features are chronic joint swelling, duration longer than 6 weeks, age under 16 years, and exclusion of another defined cause.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because JIA is defined by persistent joint swelling for more than 6 weeks in a child under 16 years without a defined cause.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because not all joint pain in children meets the definition of JIA; swelling, duration, age, and exclusion of other causes are required.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because raised inflammatory markers are not part of the definition of JIA and the duration threshold is longer than 2 weeks.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because exercise-related pain in a hypermobile child suggests a different benign musculoskeletal pattern, not JIA.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because night pain relieved by NSAIDs is not the defining feature of JIA and suggests another diagnosis.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
